column1: # One ISO per row, pinned by SHA-256. tools/coverage/corpus-fetch.sh fetches
# the harness boots each one and the scorecard reports it.
#   id        short stable name; the scorecard row and the harness's file name
#   tier      A, B or C (roadmap Section 2)
#   family    what the ISO is, for the scorecard; not what family.c says
#   sha256    of the file as published
#   file      the name it is stored under in the corpus directory
#   source    an https URL, or local:<note> for media with no stable public
#             URL (Windows, a superseded snapshot); those are copied in by hand
#             or with --local DIR and still verified against sha256
# Rows are added as a family is worked on. A row is removed only when its URL
# dies and a successor is pinned in its place.
# A few upstreams publish only a rolling name (bazzite), so the URL serves a
# different image once they cut a release and the pinned hash stops matching.
# That is the behaviour we want rather than a defect: corpus-fetch.sh refuses
# the new image loudly instead of quietly measuring something else, and the
# Hiren's is Tier C, not A: the project's last release is 1.0.8 (2024) and
# its Windows 10 1809-era bootmgr faults on firmware that write-protects
# loader pages, as a bare CD with nothing of ours in the chain (measured
# 2026-09-19 under edk2 202508). Tracked, no target; Macrium's rescue disc
